summary: Rand describes how it uses remote job entry on the network. Users build a job deck in the Rand file system, send it to UCLA's remote job service with an access program, and monitor the job's status. A sample session is included.

plainLanguage.summary: Rand's RJS Access Program lets a user submit a job to UCLA's Remote Job Service. The user can check progress and retrieve printed output through the same program.

subtitle: Instructions for using Rand's program to submit work to UCLA's Remote Job Service.

tldr.problem: A user at a site without direct Remote Job Service access needed a way to submit jobs to UCLA over the Network.
tldr.mechanism: A user logs in to Rand's PDP-10, runs the RJS Access Program, sends a job file, checks its status, and retrieves printer output.
tldr.outcome: RFC 307 documents a working procedure and sample session for RJSAP connecting to UCLA's RJS.

sections.title: The Rand-to-UCLA Connection
sections.content:
RFC 307 describes how a user at Rand could use a PDP-10 program to access the Remote Job Service on UCLA's IBM 360/91. The user prepares a job source deck in the Rand file system and asks the RJS Access Program (RJSAP) to send it.

Users at other Network sites could also log in to the Rand PDP-10 and run RJSAP if their host did not provide RJS access.
sections.plainLanguage: The user prepares a job file at Rand and sends it to UCLA's remote service. The Rand program provides the connection and commands for working with that service.

sections.title: Starting RJSAP and Sending Work
sections.content:
The user starts RJSAP by entering RJS at the TENEX executive. The program checks whether the user's login information is listed for a valid RJS terminal ID, then attempts to connect to UCLA and sign on that terminal.

Once connected, the user can enter a slash-prefixed command for RJS or use the S command to send a job source file.
sections.plainLanguage: RJSAP checks the user's access and then connects to UCLA. The user can submit an existing job file or send an operator command.

sections.title: Checking Status and Retrieving Output
sections.content:
The program includes commands for help, sending a job, retrieving printer output, checking transmission status, and quitting. The PR command sends printer output to a chosen file or device, while R reports record counts for job input and printer output.

The sample session shows a job move through queued and execution states before its print output is retrieved.
sections.plainLanguage: After submission, the user can ask for job status and request the resulting print output. The example demonstrates these steps from login through quit.
